issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Slipping, delayed or harsh shifts, dropping into neutral, stuck in one gear, a flashing overdrive or check engine light, or no reverse. Some owners went through several transmissions.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic in the Sephia had a high complaint rate. Kia set up a remanufactured transmission program for the Sephia and later released a transmission computer logic change.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition and have the codes read. If it slips or won't engage, avoid driving it far. A used or remanufactured transmission is usually the most practical repair at this age.

issues.t: Shifter stuck in Park
issues.sym: The gear lever won't move out of Park, or feels stiff and sticky, even with your foot on the brake.
issues.why: This was the most common automatic transmission complaint on the 2000 Sephia. A dealer told one owner dirt and water get into the shift linkage past a seal; the shift lock or brake switch can also be at fault.
issues.next: Check that the brake lights work, then use the shift-lock release slot near the shifter to move it out of Park. Have the shift cable, linkage and shift lock checked and lubricated.

issues.t: Engine stalls or dies while driving
issues.sym: The engine shuts off at speed, when slowing, turning or braking, sometimes with the check engine light on. Steering and brakes get heavy until it restarts.
issues.why: Stalling is one of the most reported Sephia problems in every year. Causes found include failing coils, crankshaft sensors, fuel pump wiring and idle problems, and many dealers could not repeat it.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Treat stalling as a safety risk. Have the codes read and check whether the fuel pump wiring recalls were done (1998-1999). Ignition coils and the crankshaft sensor are common suspects.

issues.t: Hard starting or stalling from a bad crankshaft sensor
issues.sym: Long cranking before the engine starts, or the engine stalls and won't restart for a while.
issues.why: Consumer Guide lists a faulty crankshaft position sensor on the 1.8L as a known cause of hard starting and stalling on these years.
issues.next: Have the crankshaft sensor tested, especially if the tachometer drops to zero when it stalls.

issues.t: Fuel pump wiring can corrode and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or cuts out, or the car won't start, often after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Two connectors that feed the fuel pump could corrode from moisture, and a fuel pump ground could loosen and overheat. Either one starves the pump of current. Kia replaced and relocated the connectors and repaired the ground.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have a Kia dealer check that both fuel pump wiring recalls were done on your VIN.

issues.t: Fuel sprays back at the pump (recall)
issues.sym: The pump nozzle clicks off early, and gas spits back out of the filler neck, sometimes onto you.
issues.why: A refueling vapor valve could close before the tank was full, so drivers kept pumping and fuel came back out. Kia replaced the valve, and NHTSA investigated more spitback reports.
issues.next: Fill slowly and stop at the first click. Have a Kia dealer confirm the valve recall was done.

issues.t: Front seat belt buckle may falsely latch (recall)
issues.sym: The buckle clicks but the latch plate pulls out with a tug, or the belt comes unbuckled.
issues.why: Front seat belt buckles could seem latched when they were not. Kia recalled them and replaced the front buckles.
issues.next: Tug the belt after every buckle-up. Have a Kia dealer check that the buckle recall was done.

issues.t: Front seat belt can click without latching (recall)
issues.sym: The front belt clicks but pulls loose when you tug on it.
issues.why: Kia recalled more front seat belt buckles that could make a latching click without being latched. Dealers replace both front buckles.
issues.next: Pull on the belt after buckling. Ask a Kia dealer whether the buckle recall was done.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can disconnect (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop moving or one arm slips on the glass, especially with snow or ice on the windshield.
issues.why: A wiper link could pop off the motor under load, and some wiper arm nuts were not tight. Kia replaced the link and tightened the nuts.
issues.next: If the wipers quit in bad weather, pull over safely. Have a Kia dealer confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Hazard lights and turn signals may stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The turn signals or hazard flashers don't work or work only some of the time.
issues.why: Kia recalled hazard switches with a poor electrical contact that could kill the turn signals and hazard lights.
issues.next: Use hand signals until it's fixed and have a Kia dealer replace the hazard switch under the recall.

issues.t: Dashboard lifts, warps or separates
issues.sym: The top of the dash bulges, curls up or comes loose near the windshield, and the defroster clears the glass poorly.
issues.why: Many owners reported the dash panel lifting, peeling or warping, often near the defroster vents. Some repairs under warranty failed again later.
issues.next: Make sure the defroster still clears the windshield. A dash panel replacement or a used dash fixes it; a cover helps with looks only.

issues.t: Brake pads and rotors wear out early
issues.sym: Squealing or grinding, a pulsing pedal, and front pads and rotors that need replacing every few thousand miles.
issues.why: Consumer Guide notes premature pad and rotor wear on every Sephia year, and Kia released a front brake pad design change. Brakes are the top complaint category for several years.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected at every tire rotation. Use quality pads and replace rotors that are below minimum thickness.

issues.t: ABS light or soft brake pedal
issues.sym: The ABS light comes on, the pedal feels soft or sinks, or stops take longer than they should.
issues.why: Owners filed many complaints about ABS faults and reduced braking on the Sephia.
issues.next: If the pedal sinks or the brake light is on, have it checked before driving further. Check the fluid level and have ABS codes read.

issues.t: Weak alternator lets the battery die
issues.sym: Dim lights, a battery light, repeated dead batteries, or everything shutting off while driving.
issues.why: RepairPal reports Kia supplied an improved alternator to replace weak originals, and Kia issued a charging system upgrade bulletin.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested before buying another battery. Ask a Kia dealer about the alternator upgrade.

issues.t: No crank from a cracked flex plate
issues.sym: The starter whirs or clunks but the engine doesn't turn, sometimes with a knocking from the bottom of the engine.
issues.why: RepairPal owners report cracked flex plates (the plate that connects the engine to the automatic transmission). The starter can't engage a broken ring gear.
issues.next: Have the starter area inspected for a cracked flex plate before replacing the starter.

issues.t: Battery or starter cable can chafe and short
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the engine bay, a sudden no-start, or a fire.
issues.why: NHTSA looked into engine compartment fires where the starter cable rubbed through, mostly after service near the cable. Kia ran a campaign for cars built before January 2000 and another to check the battery cable touching the transmission dipstick.
issues.next: If you smell burning or see smoke, turn the car off and get out. Have the battery and starter cables checked for rubbing.

issues.t: Transmission cooler line leaks at the radiator
issues.sym: Red fluid dripping near the front of the car, low transmission fluid, or shifting problems.
issues.why: NHTSA received complaints about transmission oil cooler lines leaking where they join the radiator.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and have the cooler line fittings inspected. Low fluid can ruin the transmission.

issues.t: Gas smell from fuel vapor hoses
issues.sym: A raw gas smell around the car or through the vents.
issues.why: Kia replaced the fuel vapor hoses and pipes at the tank on 1.8L cars in a campaign, and owners reported gas smells.
issues.next: Don't ignore a gas smell. Have the hoses at the tank checked and ask a Kia dealer whether the campaign was done.

issues.t: A/C stops cooling from a leaking suction hose
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm after losing its charge.
issues.why: Kia issued a bulletin for the A/C suction hose on these years.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested; replacing the hose and recharging usually fixes it.

issues.t: Front axle or CV joint breaks
issues.sym: Clicking when turning, vibration while accelerating, or a sudden loss of drive.
issues.why: Owners reported front axle shafts and CV joints failing, sometimes causing a loss of control.
issues.next: Check for torn CV boots and have clicking joints replaced before they break.

issues.t: Horn works only some of the time
issues.sym: The horn is weak, works on and off, or doesn't work at all.
issues.why: Ten owners complained to NHTSA about the horn on the 2000 Sephia; the cause was not identified.
issues.next: Have the horn, relay and steering wheel contacts checked. A working horn is a safety item.

issues.t: Check engine light and misfire from bad ignition coils
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough running, hesitation, or loss of power.
issues.why: Owners and mechanics traced running problems to failed ignition coils, and some replaced coil packs more than once.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replace the coil and check the plug wires and plugs.

issues.t: Airbag warning light or airbag concerns
issues.sym: The airbag light stays on or comes on at random. Owners also reported airbags not deploying in crashes.
issues.why: Owners filed many airbag complaints for these years, from warning lights to frontal airbags not deploying.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read right away. With the light on, the airbags may not work.

issues.t: Parking brake cable or lever fails
issues.sym: The parking brake won't hold, the lever feels loose, or it pulls up too far.
issues.why: Owners reported parking brake cables pulling out of their anchors and levers breaking.
issues.next: Don't rely on it on a hill until fixed. Have the cable and rear brakes adjusted or replaced.

issues.t: Turn signal switch fails
issues.sym: Turn signals stop working or work only on one side.
issues.why: NHTSA received complaints about turn signal switches failing, and Kia issued a turn signal circuit diagnosis bulletin.
issues.next: Check the bulbs first, then have the switch and flasher tested.
